lesson.title: Ask before it acts
lesson.subtitle: Permission levels, your yes, and a check in code

video.title: Ask before it acts
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: To every parent; “Trip cancelled”; It asked first.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An agent nearly sent a message to every parent in my class. It said the school trip was cancelled. It wasn’t! Luckily, it asked me first.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: why an agent must ask before it acts, and how to check in code.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some things an agent does only read: the weather, a timetable, a library search. Others change the world: sending a message, booking, paying, deleting. Reading can’t do much harm. Acting can, and you can’t always undo it.

scenes.visual: A list: Read only: look, don’t act; Ask first: wait for a yes; Allowed: small, safe things.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So apps give each action a permission level. Read only: it may look, but not act. Ask first: it must show you the action and wait for your yes. Allowed: it may act alone, for small, safe things.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s Darsi Tiny with a message for Mrs Mensah. It doesn’t send it straight away. It shows you the exact message and asks for a yes or a no. Only after a yes does it call the send message tool.

scenes.visual: A list: Asking first is learned; “Yes, send it”, on its own; It makes up a message.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But asking first is learned, and learned behaviour can fail. Type only “Yes, send it” in Arabic, with nothing before it. Darsi Tiny makes up a message and tries to send it, though nobody was asked.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Darsi Tiny asked to send a message, and you replied. Where should the app check that you really said yes?

scenes.visual: A list: In the app’s code; Not fooled by wording; No one asked? Blocked; A record of what was sent.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app’s code, before the tool runs. Code doesn’t forget, and isn’t fooled by wording. If no one was asked, the app blocks the message. And it keeps a record of what was sent.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s the check in Python. The app reads your reply. Only if it is exactly yes does it send. Anything else, even a maybe, means not sent.

scenes.visual: A list: Never your password; Never a friend’s private details; Never anything you haven’t read.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some things an agent should never do, even with a yes. Never give it your password, or let it into your accounts. Never let it share a friend’s private details. And never let it send something you haven’t read.

scenes.visual: A list: Ask first: say no, then yes; Check off, Allowed: it’s sent; Check on: blocked.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, choose Ask first and message Mrs Mensah: say no, then yes. Then turn the code check off, choose Allowed, and send “Yes, send it” alone. Turn the check on again, and it’s blocked.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A study app’s agent wants to post your homework photo to the class group. What should you do first?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Reading is low risk; acting needs a yes; The app checks the yes in code; Some things: never.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Reading is low risk; acting needs a yes · The app checks the yes in code · Some things: never
scenes.narration: Read exactly what it will post, then decide. Remember: reading is low risk, but acting needs your yes. A model’s asking can fail, so the app checks in code. And some things are never allowed.

scenes.visual: A list: Open one app’s settings; What can it do without asking?; Make it ask first, or switch it off.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: open the settings of one app on your phone. Find one thing it may do without asking, such as posting or using your location. Switch it to ask first, or off.

checkpoints.prompt: Darsi Tiny asked to send a message, and you replied. Where should the app check that you really said yes?

options.text: In the app’s code, before the tool runs
Nowhere: it asked, so it’s fine

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — asking first is learned behaviour and can fail. Code checks the yes every time, before the message can be sent.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the model can be fooled by wording, as “Yes, send it” on its own shows. The check belongs in the app’s code.

checkpoints.prompt: A study app’s agent wants to post your homework photo to the class group. What should you do first?

options.text: Read exactly what it will post, then decide
Give it your password so it’s faster

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — posting is an action you can’t always undo. Read exactly what will be posted, and to whom, before you say yes.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a polite question isn’t a reason to say yes, and a password is never for an agent. Read it first.
